skill.name: nestjs-feature-audit
skill.description: Compare one NestJS feature with a documented roadmap at a specific Git revision. Report implementation evidence, missing work, legacy code, bugs, and blockers without implementing fixes.
skill.summary: Audit NestJS feature completeness against roadmap requirements with revision-specific evidence.
skill.author: amirtaherkhani

security_audit.summary: All 35 static findings are false positives: Markdown backticks were mistaken for execution, and a reporting heading was mistaken for system reconnaissance. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in the reviewed files. The workflow includes remote fetch, branch switching, and fast-forward updates, with explicit worktree safeguards and no automatic fixes or publication.

content.user_title: Audit NestJS Features Against Their Roadmaps
content.value_statement: Source code alone cannot establish whether a NestJS feature satisfies its roadmap. This skill compares requirements with revision-specific evidence and reports completed work, gaps, legacy paths, bugs, and blockers.
actual_capabilities: Record the audited branch, commit, worktree state, remote revision, and freshness status.
Find roadmap candidates and stop when no clear, authoritative feature target is available.
Trace roadmap requirements to source, tests, configuration, migrations, contracts, and available runtime evidence.
Classify requirements as verified, partial, absent, superseded, broken, blocked, or not verifiable.
Produce four report sections covering implementation, missing work, legacy code, and bugs or blockers.
Separate implemented source from unverified rollout requirements and document the next required proof.
limitations: Requires Git, a NestJS repository, and a clear roadmap in repository documentation or supplied by the user.
Remote freshness verification requires network access; unavailable remotes require explicit acceptance of a local snapshot.
Runtime, deployment, and external-system claims remain unverified without safe access and supporting evidence.
Does not implement fixes, publish changes, deploy, or edit roadmaps as part of an audit alone.

use_cases.title: Check Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Compare a feature on a release branch with its acceptance plan and identify missing evidence before approval.

use_cases.title: Review Migration Progress
use_cases.description: Identify active legacy paths, replacement coverage, and rollout prerequisites against a documented migration roadmap.

use_cases.title: Plan Acceptance Validation
use_cases.description: Map roadmap requirements to tests and observed behavior, then list the checks needed to resolve unverified items.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the payments feature against its documented roadmap on main. Return the evidence-backed report without implementing fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish feature completeness on the default branch.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Release Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit subscriptions on branch release/subscriptions against the documented acceptance plan. Record revision freshness and cite evidence for each requirement. Do not implement fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare a named release revision with its requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit internal-events against its migration roadmap on main. Separate replacement code, active legacy paths, and production cutover prerequisites. Report exit evidence without deploying.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: distinguish source migration progress from rollout completion.

prompt_templates.title: Build Detailed Acceptance Traceability
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit refunds on branch release/refunds using the attached roadmap as the authoritative target. Trace each acceptance condition across source, wiring, tests, configuration, and available runtime evidence. Deduplicate findings and identify next validation steps. Do not mutate implementation or publish changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: assess a supplied roadmap across multiple evidence sources.

output_examples.input: Audit a feature with verified validation, missing retry logic, an active legacy adapter, and an unauthorized production cutover.
output: Illustrative verdict: incomplete, with a separate rollout blocker.
Implemented: request validation is wired and supported by a passing acceptance check.
Missing/Not Implemented: required retry behavior is absent from the inspected integration points.
Legacy Code: the old adapter remains active although the roadmap requires replacement.
Bugs & Blockers: production cutover requires authorization and live acceptance evidence.
Each real report item includes requirement citations, observed evidence, impact, and the next validation step.

output_examples.input: Audit invoice-reminders when documentation contains only a feature mention without acceptance conditions.
output: Roadmap required for invoice-reminders before the audit can continue.
The feature mention does not define concrete outcomes or acceptance conditions.
The response lists the actual documentation paths, search terms, and rejected candidates.
Provide a roadmap file or its contents. Implementation status is not classified until the roadmap gate passes.

best_practices: Name the feature, target branch, and authoritative roadmap before requesting comparison.
Keep the worktree clean and approve any local-snapshot exception explicitly when remote freshness cannot be verified.
Review each requirement citation and next-proof step before treating implemented source as production completion.
anti_patterns: Treating a TODO mention or existing source code as the feature roadmap.
Interpreting unavailable tests, missing runtime access, or unperformed deployment checks as verified success.
Using an audit request as permission to implement fixes, publish changes, or deploy.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Git, a NestJS repository, a feature name, and a clear roadmap. Remote updates also require network access.

faq.question: What happens when no roadmap is available?
faq.answer: It reports searched paths and terms, rejects unclear candidates, and asks for a roadmap before classifying implementation.

faq.question: Can I supply the roadmap directly?
faq.answer: Yes. A user-supplied roadmap can satisfy the gate when it identifies the feature and defines concrete requirements or acceptance conditions.

faq.question: Does the audit change Git state?
faq.answer: An explicit invocation authorizes remote fetch, branch switching, and fast-forward preparation when safe. Dirty, detached, or in-progress states stop automatic preparation.

faq.question: Will it fix findings or deploy the feature?
faq.answer: No. Fixes require explicit authorization and a separate implementation phase. Publication, deployment, and roadmap edits require their own authorization.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for all three. Use the installed skill interface; slash-command aliases depend on host configuration.
